rows.note: Use 種 as the everyday all-purpose noun for a type or kind.

example.english: What sort of tea do you like?
example.jyutping: nei5 zung1 ji3 bin1 zung2 caa4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for arranging things into an order or sequence.

example.jyutping: zoeng1 di1 man4 gin6 on3 jat6 kei4 paai4 hou2

rows.note: Use this specifically when separating items into groups according to their type or other criteria.

example.english: We sort the rubbish into categories to make recycling easier.
example.traditional: 我哋將啲垃圾分類，方便回收。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 zoeng1 di1 laap6 saap3 fan1 leoi6 fong1 bin6 wui4 sau1

rows.note: Use 呢種人 for a person belonging to the particular kind being discussed.

example.english: I’m most afraid of this sort of person.
example.jyutping: ngo5 zeoi3 paa3 ni1 zung2 jan4

rows.note: Use 好人 when someone is called “a good sort.”

example.english: He’s a really good sort and is willing to help me move house.
example.traditional: 佢真係好人，肯幫我搬屋。
example.jyutping: keoi5 zan1 hai6 hou2 jan4 hang2 bong1 ngo5 bun1 uk1

rows.note: Use 衰人 when someone is called “a bad sort.”

example.english: You’re such a bad sort—you ate all my crisps!
example.traditional: 你真係衰人，食晒我啲薯片！
example.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 seoi1 jan4 sik6 saai3 ngo5 di1 syu4 pin2
